context:
This benchmark has 1821 lines of existing DataFrame operations code. The work is
audit + integration + gap-filling, not greenfield.

Follow the write_primitives operations manager pattern for PySpark catalog/lakehouse
operations (stateful, sequential). For schema introspection operations that are
independent and stateless (df.schema, df.describe()), consider using the QueryRegistry
pattern instead - this enables the standard DataFrame runner to execute them.

A hybrid approach may be best: QueryRegistry for Tier 1 schema introspection
(works on all platforms), operations manager for Tier 2/3 catalog+lakehouse
(PySpark only). The benchmark class exposes both via get_dataframe_queries()
(returns Tier 1 registry) and get_dataframe_operations() (returns Tier 2/3 manager).

Expect ~25-30% coverage in DataFrame mode vs SQL mode. This is acceptable because
many SQL metadata queries (INFORMATION_SCHEMA, ACL, views) are inherently SQL
constructs with no DataFrame equivalent.
description:
Complete and integrate the existing DataFrame operations module for the Metadata
Primitives benchmark, enabling schema introspection benchmarking on Polars, PySpark,
Pandas, and other DataFrame platforms.

Metadata Primitives tests database metadata introspection - INFORMATION_SCHEMA queries,
SHOW/DESCRIBE/PRAGMA commands, and catalog operations - using 62 SQL queries across
10 categories: schema (9), column (8), stats (6), query (4), wide table (5), view
hierarchy (4), complex type (5), large catalog (6), constraint (4), and ACL (11).

A substantial dataframe_operations.py already exists (1821 lines) with:
- MetadataOperationType enum (13+ operation types across 4 categories)
- MetadataOperationCategory enum (SCHEMA, CATALOG, LAKEHOUSE, COMPLEXITY)
- OPERATION_CATEGORIES mapping dict
- Platform-specific support levels (all platforms for schema, PySpark for catalog,
  PySpark+Delta/Iceberg for lakehouse metadata)

Unlike SQL metadata introspection (which queries INFORMATION_SCHEMA), DataFrame
metadata operations use native DataFrame API: df.schema, df.dtypes, df.describe(),
df.columns, len(df), and platform-specific catalog APIs (spark.catalog.listTables()).

The benchmark has 3 tiers of DataFrame support:
1. Schema introspection: ALL platforms (Polars, Pandas, PySpark, DataFusion, etc.)
2. Catalog operations: PySpark with configured catalog only
3. Lakehouse metadata: PySpark + Delta Lake/Iceberg only

anti_patterns.dont: attempt to implement INFORMATION_SCHEMA queries in DataFrame mode
anti_patterns.why: DataFrames access metadata through native API (df.schema, spark.catalog), not SQL catalog tables

anti_patterns.dont: force 100% query parity with SQL mode
anti_patterns.instead: document the expected coverage gap clearly
anti_patterns.why: ACL, view hierarchy, and constraint queries are inherently SQL-only

anti_patterns.dont: rewrite the existing 1821-line module from scratch

work_units.notes:
Read benchbox/core/metadata_primitives/dataframe_operations.py (1821 lines) thoroughly.
Compare against the 62 SQL queries in catalog/queries.yaml.

Create a mapping table across 3 tiers:

Tier 1 - Schema introspection (ALL platforms):
- list_columns -> df.columns
- get_dtypes -> df.dtypes / df.schema
- describe_stats -> df.describe()
- row_count -> len(df) / df.count()
- column_count -> len(df.columns)
Map which of the 62 SQL queries correspond to these operations.

Tier 2 - Catalog operations (PySpark only):
- list_databases -> spark.catalog.listDatabases()
- list_tables -> spark.catalog.listTables()
- table_exists -> spark.catalog.tableExists()
Map SQL INFORMATION_SCHEMA queries to catalog API calls.

Tier 3 - Lakehouse metadata (PySpark + Delta/Iceberg):
- table_history -> DeltaTable.history()
- table_detail -> DeltaTable.detail()
Map SQL queries to format-specific metadata APIs.

Identify:
- Which operations are fully implemented?
- Which are stubs?
- Which SQL queries have no DataFrame equivalent (e.g., ACL queries)?
work_units.summary: Audit existing dataframe_operations.py - map SQL queries to DataFrame operations, identify gaps

work_units.notes:
Ensure Tier 1 operations work across all platforms:

Expression family (Polars, DataFusion, PySpark):
- Schema access via ctx.get_table(name).schema
- Column listing via ctx.get_table(name).columns
- Statistics via describe() or platform-specific stats methods

Pandas family (Pandas, Modin, cuDF, Dask):
- df.dtypes, df.describe(), df.info(), df.columns, len(df)
- df.memory_usage() for size statistics
- df.nunique() for cardinality

These are the most broadly supported operations and should work on all 8
DataFrame platforms. Implement as DataFrameQuery objects with expression_impl
and pandas_impl, even though these are metadata operations - the QueryRegistry
pattern enables integration with the standard DataFrame runner.
work_units.summary: Complete schema introspection operations for all DataFrame platforms

work_units.notes:
Tier 2 (PySpark catalog):
- Implement using spark.catalog.* API
- listDatabases(), listTables(), listColumns(), tableExists()
- These require a SparkSession with a configured catalog

Tier 3 (PySpark + Delta/Iceberg):
- DeltaTable.forPath(spark, path).history() / .detail()
- Iceberg snapshot listing via table properties

Define comprehensive skip lists:
- SKIP_FOR_DATAFRAME: ACL queries (GRANT/REVOKE timing), view hierarchy queries
  (DataFrames don't have views), constraint queries (FK/PK are schema-level)
- SKIP_FOR_POLARS/PANDAS: Catalog and lakehouse operations
- SKIP_FOR_EXPRESSION_FAMILY: Catalog operations (except PySpark)

Many of the 62 SQL queries are SQL-specific (INFORMATION_SCHEMA, SHOW commands)
and will be skipped. Document the expected coverage: ~15-20 operations in
DataFrame mode vs 62 SQL queries.
work_units.summary: Complete catalog and lakehouse operations for PySpark and define skip lists

work_units.notes:
Integration:
1. Add get_dataframe_queries() or get_dataframe_operations() to
   MetadataPrimitivesBenchmark - decide which pattern based on w1 audit.
   If operations are independent (stateless introspection), use QueryRegistry.
   If operations are sequential/stateful, use operations manager.
2. Set supports_dataframe: True in benchmark_registry.py
3. Ensure TPC-H schema tables are loaded before metadata introspection runs
   (metadata queries inspect the loaded tables)
4. Handle complexity testing (wide tables, large catalogs) - may need to
   generate test structures in DataFrame mode too

Tests (tests/unit/core/metadata_primitives/test_dataframe_operations.py):
- Test MetadataOperationType enum values
- Test per-platform capability detection
- Test schema introspection operations on small synthetic DataFrames
- Test skip list correctness (Polars skips catalog ops, etc.)
- Test operation categories mapping
- Mark tests @pytest.mark.fast
work_units.summary: Wire up MetadataPrimitivesBenchmark class, registry, and add unit tests
